from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

    def construct(self):

            "Neurons act like locks for specific patterns.",

            dot.move_to(layer1[i].get_center())
            
        nodes2 = VGroup(*[Dot(color="#00FF00") for _ in range(3)])
        for i, dot in enumerate(nodes2):
            dot.move_to(layer2[i].get_center())

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Inputs activate dedicated fact neurons.", "Information projects to output space.", "Weights allow surgical model editing."]
        self.setup_layout("The Memory Retrieval Process", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define semantic colors
        INPUT_COLOR = "#ADD8E6"  # Light Blue
        NEURON_COLOR = "#FFD700" # Gold
        
        # Prepare animation objects
        input_token = Circle(radius=0.4, color=INPUT_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.6)
        neuron_cluster = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.1, color=NEURON_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.8).move_to(self.grid[pos]) for pos in ["C3", "C4", "D3", "D4"]])
        output_concept = Dot(color=WHITE, radius=0.2).scale(2)
        
        # Labels
        input_label = Text("Input", font_size=20, color=INPUT_COLOR).next_to(input_token, DOWN)
        neuron_label = Text("Fact Neurons", font_size=20, color=NEURON_COLOR).next_to(neuron_cluster, UP)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(INPUT_COLOR)
        self.play(FadeIn(input_token), Write(input_label))
        self.play(input_token.animate.move_to(self.grid["C2"]))
        self.play(FadeIn(neuron_cluster), Write(neuron_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(NEURON_COLOR)
        self.play(input_token.animate.set_color(NEURON_COLOR), run_time=1)
        self.play(input_token.animate.move_to(self.grid["E5"]))
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(input_token.copy(), output_concept.move_to(self.grid["E5"])))
        self.play(FadeIn(output_concept))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.play(Indicate(neuron_cluster))
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: How Multilayer Perceptrons (MLP) Store Facts in Transformers

sections.title: The Analogy: Library vs. Book Content
sections.content: Define the Transformer architecture's duality: Attention mechanisms represent 'retrieval' (pointing to information), while the MLP layers represent 'knowledge storage' (the content itself).
sections.example: Imagine a library. Attention is the 'Index/Catalog' that helps you find the right shelf, while the MLP is the 'Book' where the actual facts are written on the pages.

sections.title: The MLP Mechanism: Key-Value Memories
sections.content: Introduce the MLP as a series of weight matrices. We visualize this as a 'Key-Value' lookup table. The first linear layer acts as a 'Key' detector (pattern matching), and the second acts as a 'Value' generator (outputting the fact).
sections.example: When the model sees 'Paris', the neurons act like a lock. If the input matches the 'City' key, the neurons fire, outputting the stored value 'France'.

sections.title: Visualizing Weights as Knowledge
sections.content: Explain how facts are 'distributed' across neurons. Use a graphical concept: instead of one neuron = one fact, represent it as a 'constellation' of weights. Activation is like a spotlight hitting a specific pattern of neurons.
sections.example: Visual representation of a neural network layer where activating a specific subset of nodes lights up the path representing 'The capital of France is Paris'.

sections.title: The Memory Retrieval Process
sections.content: Summarize the feed-forward cycle: Input vector -> Activation of 'Fact Neurons' -> Projection into output space. Connect this to the concept of 'Model Editing' (how researchers can change facts by altering weights).
sections.example: If a robot mistakenly thinks 'The capital of Japan is Tokyo', we can surgically modify the weights in the MLP layer to 'overwrite' the specific fact-node, changing its output to a new correction.

sections.title: Conclusion and Limitations
sections.content: Conclude by emphasizing that MLPs function as a 'compressed database'. Note that this storage is fuzzy and associative rather than a rigid database.
sections.example: A 'Cloud' of connected dots representing knowledge; it's robust and associative—knowing 'France' is in Europe helps the model infer other facts linked through the same weighted paths.
